messages.subject: Re: Error ellipse features
messages.body_plain:
I stated the semi.major/semi.minor relations inversely here:

Argos.semi.major is the larger of the COV matrix eigenvalues (variances) multiplied by 2 and then square rooted (in meters).
Argos.semi.minor is the smaller of the COV matrix eigenvalues (variances) multiplied  by 2 and then square rooted (in meters).

I apologize for the error,
Chris

> Argos.orientation is the counter-clockwise angle between the the major axis (of largest variance) and north.
> Argos.semi.major is the larger of the COV matrix eigenvalues (variances) divided by 2 and then square rooted (in meters).

messages.subject: Re: combining location data from multiple methods
messages.subject_clean: combining location data from multiple methods
messages.body_plain:
Hi Marie,

Yes, my suggestion is to import the different device data in separate files so that as.telemetry() can interpret the error information correctly.
Then get their error information settled, such as calibrating or placing priors on the GPS error. In the simplest case when the GPS errors are not substantial and the sampling rate is not too high, you might be able to get away with uere(GPS.DATA) <- 0.
Finally, merge them together with tbind(), which should merge the error information and sort the timestamps.
If you run into any issues, please let me know.

Best,
Chris

Hi Kimberley,

The advantage of using continuous-time models/methods is that you don't need to worry about what the best time interval is. You will want to use all of the data.

As for the file formatting issues, when I try to download the attached CSV, I get only three rows of data with mismatch columns? In your errors, fread is also complaining about basic file formatting as well.
Have you tried getting your data onto Movebank? You don't have to make the data public to store it there.

Best,
Chris

hi,

I'm new to spatial analysis, and have been mapping my data using the tmap and ggplot2 packages (successfully importing, projecting and plotting my data). However, when I try to extend into the ctmm, I'm having problems even importing my data correctly.

Here is my code; (just for one animal at the moment - I dropped the extra variables to see if this was causing any issues). NB ALLmales is a data frame that I've successfully converted to a spatial data frame for other packages.

GRG <- filter(ALLmales, collarid == "Garango")
GRG <- subset(GRG, select = -c(HDOP, SPEED, HEADING, HACCURACY,TIMETOFIX, RETRIES))
GRG<- rename(GRG, timestamp = DATETIME)
GRG <- rename(GRG, ID = collarid)
GRG <- as.telemetry(GRG, timezone = "UTC+03", timeformat = "auto", projection =
                            "longlat +ellps=WGS84 +datum=WGS84 +no_defs")

messages.body_plain:
Hi Vicki,

To me it looks like your timestamp column is already stored as a POSIXct and not a character value, so the timeformat and timezone arguments are going to be ignored as there is no character -> POSIXct conversion to do on import. I would make sure the timestamps are correct before as.telemetry().

Does it import without error if you remove the projection argument? ctmm requires a locally flat projection in meters, which that argument does not provide.

If that doesn't fix the issue, then please message me with some data and I can take a look.

Best,
Chris
